listenings.text: Hi Samuel, this is Diane Whitmore from Harrow and Vance in Philadelphia. I'm calling about the supply agreement for the Atlas matter. My client signs off on the commercial terms, so we are not reopening price. What we do need is clarity on two points before Friday: the scope of the indemnity, and who carries the risk if the regulator delays the licence. I'm sending you the current draft this afternoon. I handle the corporate side here, so I will be your main contact until closing. Talk soon.

Samuel, quick one before you leave. I'm passing the Atlas matter to you. You already know the client and you drafted the first lease for them last year, so you are the natural fit. The other side is American counsel, and they move fast. Two things I want from you on the first call. Say clearly what you handle, so nobody wastes time on the wrong person. And set the agenda yourself before they set it for you. If you open the call, you control what gets discussed. Good luck.

items.situation: The counterparty asks what you cover on your side. Answer in two sentences: your practice, then this month.
tips: I handle contract and corporate work.
At the moment I am handling the Atlas matter.

items.situation: You want the meeting to follow your order, not theirs. Propose the agenda.
tips: Before we start, may I suggest an agenda?
Let us take the indemnity first, and the regulatory risk second.

items.situation: The other side uses a term you did not catch. Ask about it without losing authority.
tips: Could you clarify the scope of that clause?
Sorry, could you go over that once more?

items.situation: They push for a decision you are not ready to give today.
tips: Let me come back to you on that before Friday.
I would rather check the draft before I commit.

items.situation: You disagree with the risk allocation. Say so politely, and hold your position.
tips: I see your point, but I would put that risk on the supplier.
We are not comfortable carrying a regulatory delay.
